newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech parliament backs bond to fund flood relief.
newsitem.headline: Czech parliament backs bond to fund flood relief.

text.p: The Czech parliament on Friday approved a government proposal to issue up to five billion crowns ($150.3 million) in domestic government bonds to raise emergency funds for flood relief.
The bonds will be issued to private individuals and institutions.

The government also wants parliament to transfer three billion crowns in proceeds from privatisation of smaller businesses completed earlier this decade for the flood relief effort. The cabinet on Wednesday approved just over one billion crowns from various sources at its disposal for emergency relief.

At least 23 have died in the floods, which began last weekend in the eastern part of the country after torrential rain, according to official reports published by the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes on Friday. Dozens of people have been reported missing.

The floods have also hit parts of neighbouring Poland, Slovakia and Austria, forcing tens of thousands out of their homes and causing heavy damage to homes, buildings, and infrastructure. ($ = 33.26 Czech Crowns)
